suite_title: Hero Demo: Background Worker Thread Race Condition
description: Flagship benchmark demonstrating a thread scheduling race condition in a background job processor. The test uses a fixed time.sleep() instead of proper event synchronization, causing intermittent failures that spike sharply under CPU contention.
root_cause: The test asserts worker.is_completed after a fixed time.sleep(0.009) instead of using the worker's threading.Event-based wait_for_completion() method. Under CPU contention from background burner threads, the worker thread is starved of scheduling slots and takes 50-200ms+ instead of ~8-15ms, causing the assertion to fire before the worker finishes.

expected_behavior.baseline: Low failure rate (~2-8%). The worker usually finishes 8 SHA-256 iterations in ~8-15ms, beating the 9ms sleep on a quiet machine.
expected_behavior.shuffle_order: Similar to baseline. Test execution order does not affect this single-test race.
expected_behavior.seed_change: Similar to baseline. Random seeds do not affect threading behavior.
expected_behavior.clock_shift: Similar to baseline. Clock skew shifts time.time() but not time.sleep() duration.
expected_behavior.network_cut: Similar to baseline. No network operations in this test.
expected_behavior.cpu_half_cores: Moderate increase (~10-25%). Fewer cores increases thread scheduling contention.
expected_behavior.cpu_heavy_load: SHARP SPIKE (>25-60%). Background CPU burner threads compete for GIL and OS scheduling, starving the worker thread.

naive_quick_fix.description: Increases time.sleep from 0.009s to 0.050s. Passes baseline (0% failures) but still fails under cpu_heavy_load (>25% failure rate) because it's still a fixed-sleep race condition.

certified_real_fix.description: Replaces time.sleep with worker.wait_for_completion(timeout=5.0) using threading.Event.wait(). Achieves 0% failures on BOTH baseline AND cpu_heavy_load because the OS kernel handles thread wake-up.
